rules: A volatility-term-structure ratio (long-window TS_STD over short-window TS_STD of one field) crossed with that same field's own short TS_DELTA scored this round's top fitness (6.583) as pure price, beating every fundamental-crossed accept. Do not treat this shape as low-value filler like plain OHLC levels/returns.

Swapping only the top-level combinator (* vs -) between two otherwise-identical CS_RANK legs still shares the full subtree (4 nodes) and gets rejected. Change a leg's field, window, or wrapper too, not just how the legs combine.

Swapping a single OHLC leaf while leaving an identical guarded denominator/wrapper in place shares nearly the whole tree (6-7+ nodes). Vary two structural pieces at once when reusing an archived shape, not just the one leaf.

A 252-day window failed coverage (0.874) on a plain price field ($close), matching the fundamental failure range exactly. Treat ~252-day lookbacks as a coverage risk for any field, not just sparse fundamentals.

Every cheap_screen reject this round was a price/return/volume-only combination (|t| 0.17-0.57, 4 for 4). A fundamental leg is still required to clear the cheap screen at all, not just to score well later.

Adding an extra multiplicative TS_RANK(volume) factor to an existing two-leg expression, even combined with an overall sign flip, kept correlation at 0.976 against the original. Bolting on a volume-rank multiplier is not a reliable way to decorrelate from an archived idea.

Inserting a smoothing wrapper (e.g. TS_MEAN) around just one leaf of a multi-term product, leaving the rest of the structure untouched, still shared 6 of the tree's nodes. Wrap at least two legs, or change the outer combinator too.

About a third of this round's rejects were in-run duplicates, clustered in two templates: open/high/low range-position ratios and EPS-times-dollar-volume-rank ratios. Deprioritize further variations of these two families next round.
